title: Review questions: preserve the reply boundary
summary:
- Review prefixes questions with read-only context and their canonical thread ID.
- The authoring skill instructs the answering agent to return text without editing files.
why: A question needs the correct discussion context. Answering and authoring have different responsibilities.
context: Source inspection of [devdotfast/review at cf455334](https://github.com/devdotfast/review/tree/cf455334cbe43036feb00f537777a96b06649233). Base and head are the same snapshot.

| 2 | Answering agent | Read canonical target and messages using `review threads get` | [Ask reply instructions](https://github.com/devdotfast/review/blob/cf455334cbe43036feb00f537777a96b06649233/packages/progressive-review/skills/dev-review/SKILL.md#in-app-ask-replies) |
| 3 | Answering agent | Return answer text | [Ask reply instructions](https://github.com/devdotfast/review/blob/cf455334cbe43036feb00f537777a96b06649233/packages/progressive-review/skills/dev-review/SKILL.md#in-app-ask-replies) |

<Section title="Inspect the separate feedback workflow" collapsible={true} defaultOpen={false}>

Submitted review comments use a different prompt. It directs the author to inspect canonical thread state, make requested changes, resolve addressed threads, and re-list threads before publishing.

[Submission prompt implementation](https://github.com/devdotfast/review/blob/cf455334cbe43036feb00f537777a96b06649233/packages/progressive-review/src/server/review-api.ts#L1325-L1351).

This separation is visible in the source instructions. This document does not claim that prompt text alone enforces read-only behavior.

</Section>
